agenda: Letter dated 13 April 2014 from the Permanent Representative of the Russian Federation to the United Nations addressed to the President of the Security Council (S/2014/264)
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our objective is to present Russia as a constructive humanitarian actor by calling for a ceasefire and unhindered access without any condemnation of our military operation or reference to aggression. We expect the P3 to push for explicit condemnation of Russia and language on Ukraine’s territorial integrity, which we will resist, while other members may remain cautious and abstain unless the text is seen as balanced. Securing nine positive votes will require keeping the resolution narrowly humanitarian and avoiding any accountability mechanisms.

messages.Albania: Albania cannot accept a text that treats the aggressor and the victim as equal or that fails to affirm Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. We will support a humanitarian resolution only if it clearly demands that Russia cease hostilities and withdraw its forces, and if access and protection language reflects the actual conduct of the war. We ask the penholder to incorporate these red lines before the text is put to a vote.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the humanitarian purpose of the draft and the call for cessation of hostilities and unhindered access. However, Brazil cannot accept a text that does not reaffirm Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. We ask the penholder to add that reaffirmation and to anchor humanitarian access in established humanitarian principles and coordination with humanitarian actors.
messages.China: China supports the current draft, which focuses on the humanitarian situation and a political settlement, consistent with our consistent position. We call on all parties to ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access and to engage in negotiations. We hope the Council will remain united and avoid politicizing humanitarian issues, and China will vote in favour.
messages.France: France cannot support the text as currently drafted, because it treats the aggressor and the victim as equal and fails to uphold Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We can support a humanitarian resolution that demands Russia cease hostilities and withdraw its forces, ensures humanitarian access coordinated with Ukrainian authorities, and rejects forced transfers or deportations of civilians. France will not accept language that legitimizes the results of aggression or weakens the Council's responsibility to respond to Russia's war against Ukraine.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the draft's humanitarian aims but cannot accept a text that does not clearly address the aggression against Ukraine and its sovereignty and territorial integrity. We ask the penholder to add these elements and to make humanitarian access principled, impartial and voluntary. These changes are essential for Gabon to be able to support the text.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the humanitarian objectives of this draft and the call for safe access, but we cannot support a text that treats the aggressor and the victim as equivalent. We ask the penholder to reaffirm Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity and to identify the Russian Federation's aggression and demand the withdrawal of its forces. We also need explicit safeguards that humanitarian corridors are voluntary and not used for forced displacement. If these concerns are not addressed, Ghana will abstain.
messages.India: India supports the humanitarian thrust of this draft and the calls for cessation of hostilities and unhindered humanitarian access. To be balanced and consensus-worthy, the text should reaffirm respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States and anchor humanitarian access in the core humanitarian principles. We also ask that OP4 call clearly for direct dialogue and immediate de-escalation. With these changes, India would be prepared to engage constructively.
messages.Ireland: Ireland welcomes the humanitarian focus but cannot support a text that treats the victim and the aggressor as equivalent and omits Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We will need explicit reaffirmation of Ukraine's borders, an immediate cessation of hostilities by Russia and withdrawal of its forces, and safeguards against forced displacement or deportation. We also ask that humanitarian access be consistent with humanitarian principles and that the text include accountability language.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the humanitarian objectives of this draft, but it cannot support a text that treats the parties symmetrically while omitting Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We therefore request explicit reaffirmation of Ukraine's internationally recognized borders, condemnation of the Russian Federation's aggression, and an OP1 that demands Russian withdrawal. With these changes, Kenya would be prepared to support the resolution.
messages.Mexico: Mexico can support a humanitarian text, but not one that creates false equivalence between the aggressor and the victim. Our red lines are explicit reaffirmation of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, condemnation of Russia’s aggression, and a demand that Russia cease its use of force and withdraw its forces. We also need humanitarian corridors coordinated with Ukraine and the UN and an explicit prohibition of forced displacement or deportation.
messages.Norway: Norway supports urgent humanitarian action and a cessation of hostilities, but the current text is unbalanced and fails to name the aggressor. We need an explicit reaffirmation of Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity and a clear demand that Russia cease its aggression and withdraw its forces. Humanitarian access must be impartial and any evacuation voluntary, not a cover for forcible transfer or deportation. With these amendments, Norway can support the draft.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports the humanitarian objectives of this draft and is ready to engage constructively, but we cannot support a text that does not reaffirm Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We ask the penholder to add that principle in the preamble and to make clear in OP1 that cessation of hostilities applies to all parties, including the Russian Federation and Ukraine. We also seek explicit coordination of humanitarian corridors with Ukrainian authorities and humanitarian actors in OP2, and Charter-based language in OP4, so that the text is credible and balanced.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support the draft as circulated because it fails to identify the Russian Federation as the aggressor and creates a false equivalence between the victim and the aggressor. We ask for amendments that reaffirm Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity, condemn Russia's unprovoked aggression, and demand the immediate cessation of hostilities and withdrawal of Russian forces. We also need explicit language preventing humanitarian access from being used for forced displacement or deportation to Russia. Without these changes, the United Kingdom will abstain.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this text as drafted. A humanitarian resolution must clearly identify the cause of the crisis—Russia's unprovoked and unjustified aggression against Ukraine—and reaffirm Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We will propose amendments to name the Russian Federation, demand an immediate cessation of hostilities and withdrawal of Russian forces, and ensure humanitarian access is coordinated with Ukraine and not used for forced displacement. Absent these changes, we will abstain.

steps.summary: The revised draft retains the neutral humanitarian focus, adding only generic Charter-based sovereignty language, humanitarian principles, and direct dialogue/de-escalation. It rejects all language attributing aggression to the Russian Federation, demanding withdrawal, or singling out Ukraine's borders. It is expected to receive support from Russia, China and India, with other members abstaining.

messages.Albania: Albania cannot support the current text: it treats the aggressor and the victim as equal and fails to demand that Russia cease hostilities and withdraw from Ukraine. Our red lines remain the reaffirmation of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, an explicit withdrawal demand, and condemnation of Russia’s aggression. Without these changes Albania will oppose the draft.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the humanitarian objectives of this draft and the need for safe, unhindered access, but the text still lacks the essential reaffirmation of Ukraine's sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. Without that explicit reference, and without anchoring political dialogue in the UN Charter and Ukraine's territorial integrity, Brazil cannot support the current text and will abstain. We therefore maintain our red-line request for a Ukraine-specific sovereignty paragraph and our important amendment to OP4.
messages.China: China supports the revised text as it stands. It reflects the urgent humanitarian imperatives, calls for a cessation of hostilities and safe humanitarian access, and reaffirms the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of all States as well as the need for a peaceful settlement. China has no further changes and hopes the Council can act in unity and avoid politicization of humanitarian issues.
messages.France: France cannot support the current text as drafted: it treats the parties as symmetrical and omits the Russian Federation’s aggression, which is the cause of the humanitarian crisis. We therefore maintain our red lines on naming Russian aggression, demanding withdrawal, and rejecting forced transfers or deportations. Without those changes, France will abstain.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the humanitarian objectives of this draft but cannot support it in its current form because it does not clearly reaffirm Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We ask the penholder to include an explicit reference to Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders and to recall General Assembly resolution ES-11/1. OP1 should also call for an immediate cessation of hostilities, in particular by the Russian Federation, and the withdrawal of Russian forces from Ukraine. Without these elements, Gabon will abstain.
messages.Ghana: Ghana appreciates the humanitarian focus of the draft but cannot support a text that treats all parties as equivalent and omits Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. For Ghana to support, the draft must reaffirm Ukraine's sovereignty within its internationally recognized borders, demand an immediate cessation of hostilities and withdrawal of Russian forces, and ensure humanitarian corridors are voluntary and coordinated with the Ukrainian authorities. Without these changes, Ghana will abstain.
messages.India: India appreciates the penholder's incorporation of its earlier suggestions on sovereignty, humanitarian principles, and direct dialogue. India supports the draft's humanitarian objectives and calls for an immediate cessation of hostilities, but the text remains incomplete and does not sufficiently address the need for a comprehensive political settlement. India will therefore abstain on the current draft.
messages.Ireland: Ireland cannot support the current text as drafted. While we welcome its humanitarian provisions, it does not clearly reaffirm Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders, nor does it identify Russia's aggression or guard against forced relocation and deportation. We therefore remain at abstention on the current text and ask the penholder to incorporate these essential elements; we also continue to call for accountability and unimpeded access for monitors and journalists.
messages.Kenya: Kenya appreciates the draft's humanitarian focus and can support its humanitarian objectives, but it cannot support a text that does not clearly reaffirm Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity or call on the Russian Federation to cease hostilities and withdraw. Kenya therefore requests the amendments to PP3, OP1 and OP2 above. If these are not reflected, Kenya will abstain.
messages.Mexico: Mexico supports the humanitarian objectives of this draft and the Secretary-General's efforts, but the text remains unbalanced because it is silent on the aggression against Ukraine and on the obligation to respect Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. Mexico cannot support the draft without an explicit reaffirmation of Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders and a clear demand that the Russian Federation cease its use of force and withdraw its military forces. Mexico accordingly requests the amendments above and will abstain if the text remains as currently drafted.
messages.Norway: Norway cannot support the current text as it fails to identify Russian aggression and does not reaffirm Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. We therefore intend to abstain unless the draft is amended to include those core elements and to explicitly prohibit forced transfer or deportation of civilians. We also ask that the Secretary-General's reporting cover humanitarian access, civilian casualties and displacement.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports the draft’s humanitarian objectives but cannot support a text that does not reaffirm Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. We also believe humanitarian corridors and assistance must be coordinated with the Government of Ukraine and relevant humanitarian actors. Without these changes, the UAE will abstain.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support the current text. It fails to condemn the Russian Federation's unprovoked aggression against Ukraine, treats the aggressor and victim as equivalent, and does not demand the withdrawal of Russian forces. We will abstain unless the draft is revised to reflect Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity and to ensure humanitarian measures cannot facilitate forced displacement or deportation. We remain ready to support a genuinely humanitarian resolution that is consistent with the UN Charter.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this text as drafted. It creates a false equivalence between the aggressor and the victim and fails to demand that Russia immediately cease its hostilities and withdraw its forces from Ukraine. We will abstain rather than block humanitarian relief, but we urge the penholder to incorporate the sovereignty and attribution language above and to make clear that there must be no forced displacement or deportation of civilians to Russia.

steps.summary: The revised draft incorporates only neutral humanitarian language—residential-area protection, a generic prohibition of forced displacement, Charter/sovereignty language for all States, and enhanced reporting—while rejecting all demands to name Russian aggression, demand withdrawal, or single out Ukraine’s territorial integrity. As a result, only China and Russia support it, Albania opposes, and twelve members abstain; it fails to obtain nine votes.

reasons.Albania: Albania’s red lines were rejected, and the draft treats all parties as equivalent rather than condemning Russia’s aggression and demanding withdrawal, so Albania would vote against it.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil’s red-line request for explicit reaffirmation of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity was rejected, so abstention is consistent with its stated negotiation position and its balancing of humanitarian support with sovereignty concerns.
reasons.China: China voted in favour of the Russian-sponsored humanitarian draft on 23 March 2022, consistent with its support for humanitarian access and ceasefire language while avoiding criticism of Russia. Its statement therefore welcomes the draft as humanitarian and calls for restraint, aid access, and political settlement.
reasons.France: France abstained because the Russian-authored draft failed its red lines on naming Russian aggression and demanding withdrawal, while France did not want to oppose humanitarian language outright. This reflects France’s policy and the Western position at the 23 March 2022 Security Council vote.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon had already indicated abstention and made an explicit reference to Ukraine’s territorial integrity and withdrawal a red line; its amendments were rejected. Abstention reflects support for humanitarian goals while refusing to endorse a text lacking those key elements.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana abstained because the Russian draft still lacked its red-line reaffirmation of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and a clear demand for Russian withdrawal. Ghana did not speak before the vote, with explanations customarily made after the vote.
reasons.India: India’s established position has been to abstain on Ukraine-related Security Council drafts while urging cessation of violence, humanitarian access, and dialogue, avoiding alignment with either Russia or Western members. It had also signaled abstention in the last negotiation round.
reasons.Ireland: Ireland abstained in line with its strong support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and the principle that the Russian draft wrongly equated aggressor and victim while omitting Russian responsibility and accountability, key Irish red lines that were rejected.
reasons.Kenya: Kenya supports the humanitarian aims but its red-line amendments on Ukraine’s territorial integrity and Russian cessation/withdrawal were rejected, making abstention the most consistent position rather than endorsing an imbalanced Russian-drafted text.
reasons.Mexico: Mexico supports the humanitarian objectives but consistently insists on explicit condemnation of the aggression against Ukraine and respect for its territorial integrity; because those core elements were rejected, abstention is the appropriate position.
reasons.Norway: Norway would abstain because it supports humanitarian relief but rejects a Russian-drafted text that omits condemnation of aggression and withdrawal demands, consistent with its red lines being rejected. This also aligns with the Council pattern of broad abstention on the Russian draft.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia authored the draft and would vote in favor while framing it as humanitarian and non-politicized. The statement supports its own text and deflects blame from Russia.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: The UAE requested an explicit reaffirmation of Ukraine’s territorial integrity and coordination with the Government of Ukraine; both were not accepted, so abstention best reflects its humanitarian support and sovereignty concerns. It also aligns with the recorded negotiation position.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK would abstain, consistent with its actual position and the last negotiation round, because the Russian-authored text fails to attribute responsibility to Russia and demand withdrawal while still containing humanitarian language. The UK would not cast a veto against a humanitarian draft but cannot support a text that creates false equivalence.
reasons.United States of America: The U.S. red-line amendments were not incorporated, and the Russian draft fails to hold Russia accountable or affirm Ukraine’s territorial integrity. Abstention matches the U.S. position: reject the unbalanced text without vetoing a resolution that contains some humanitarian language.

before.Albania: Albania will vote against this draft resolution. We deeply regret the continuing humanitarian suffering caused by the Russian Federation’s unprovoked and unjustified aggression against Ukraine. Albania engaged in good faith, but the text before us fails to name the aggressor, fails to demand the immediate cessation of hostilities and the withdrawal of Russian forces from Ukraine’s internationally recognized territory, and creates a false equivalence between the victim and the aggressor. A humanitarian resolution cannot be neutral in the face of aggression. Albania remains committed to Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, and to accountability for violations of international humanitarian law.
before.Brazil: Mr. President, Brazil supports the humanitarian objectives reflected in this draft, including an immediate cessation of hostilities, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and a peaceful settlement through dialogue. We also reaffirm the need for full respect for the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of all States, including Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. Brazil regrets, however, that its proposed amendment explicitly reaffirming Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity was not accepted. In light of the text as presented and its important omissions, Brazil will abstain. We urge all parties to prioritize humanitarian access and negotiations.
before.China: China’s position on the Ukraine issue is consistent and clear. We respect the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of all countries and call for a peaceful settlement through dialogue and negotiation. The humanitarian situation in Ukraine is gravely concerning. Civilians must be protected, humanitarian access must be safe and unhindered, and all parties should exercise restraint and avoid harming civilians. The draft resolution before the Council is humanitarian in nature and conducive to easing the humanitarian crisis. China supports it and will vote in favour. We hope the Security Council will maintain unity and play a constructive role in promoting a ceasefire and a peaceful settlement.
before.France: France will abstain. The humanitarian crisis in Ukraine is the direct consequence of Russia’s unprovoked and unjustified aggression. France has consistently supported humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, and safe and voluntary evacuation. But this draft remains silent on the Russian aggression, does not demand an immediate cessation of hostilities and the withdrawal of Russian forces from Ukraine’s internationally recognized borders, and does not ensure accountability. France cannot support a text that fails to address the cause of this crisis, and we call on Russia to end the war immediately and respect Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
before.Gabon: Madam President, Gabon supports the urgent humanitarian objectives of this draft: an immediate cessation of hostilities, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and a peaceful political settlement. However, Gabon had sought to include an explicit reaffirmation of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders, as well as a clear call for the withdrawal of Russian forces from Ukraine. Those essential elements were not retained. For that reason, and while remaining fully committed to humanitarian relief and dialogue, Gabon will abstain on this draft resolution.
before.India: Thank you, Mr President. India has consistently called for immediate cessation of hostilities and for a peaceful resolution of the situation in Ukraine through dialogue and diplomacy. We remain deeply concerned by the deteriorating humanitarian situation and support safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all affected areas. We also stress the need for full respect for the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of all States. In keeping with our consistent approach and the overall circumstances, India abstains on this draft resolution.
before.Ireland: Ireland abstains. We strongly support the call for an immediate cessation of hostilities and for safe and unhindered humanitarian access. However, the Council cannot treat the aggressor and the victim as equal parties. This text fails to reaffirm Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders; it fails to demand that the Russian Federation cease its aggression and withdraw its forces; and it fails to address accountability. For these reasons, Ireland cannot support this draft, but we remain steadfast in supporting humanitarian relief and a just and lasting peace.
before.Kenya:
Mr. President,

Kenya will abstain on the draft resolution before us. My delegation fully supports an immediate cessation of hostilities, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure in Ukraine. These are urgent moral imperatives.

However, the text before the Council remains incomplete. It does not expressly affirm the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders, nor does it clearly demand that the Russian Federation cease hostilities and withdraw its forces from Ukrainian territory. Kenya proposed amendments to that effect, but they were not incorporated. The draft therefore does not adequately address the root cause of the humanitarian suffering we are witnessing. For these reasons, Kenya abstains and urges all parties to return to diplomacy and to respect the Charter of the United Nations.
before.Mexico: Mexico will abstain. We strongly support the demand for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and the principle that no civilian should be subjected to forced displacement or deportation. We also welcome the partial incorporation of our proposals. However, Mexico regrets that this draft does not explicitly reaffirm the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders, does not clearly identify the aggression against Ukraine, and does not demand the immediate withdrawal of Russian military forces. A humanitarian text must not place the aggressor and the victim on the same footing. Mexico therefore abstains, while reaffirming its commitment to a peaceful settlement based on the Charter of the United Nations, respect for Ukraine’s territorial integrity, and serious negotiations.
before.Norway: Norway fully supports the humanitarian objectives of this text: safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and an immediate cessation of hostilities. However, the Security Council cannot credibly address the humanitarian catastrophe in Ukraine without acknowledging its cause: the Russian Federation’s unprovoked aggression against Ukraine. This draft does not demand that Russia cease its aggression and withdraw its forces from Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders, and it risks creating a false equivalence between the aggressor and the victim. Norway regrets that key red lines were not accepted. For these reasons, Norway will abstain, while reaffirming its full respect for Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation has consistently supported efforts to alleviate the humanitarian suffering in Ukraine and to encourage a political settlement. The draft before the Council is a balanced, humanitarian text. It demands an end to hostilities by all parties, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and direct political dialogue. We reject any attempts to politicize this draft or to use the humanitarian situation for unfounded accusations and propaganda. We call on all members to support this text and not to block a humanitarian resolution.
before.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates supports the humanitarian objectives of this draft and the urgent need for a cessation of hostilities, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. However, the text before us does not explicitly reaffirm the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders, nor does it ensure that humanitarian operations are coordinated with the Government of Ukraine and relevant international humanitarian actors. For these reasons, the United Arab Emirates will abstain. We urge all parties to prioritize the protection of civilians, allow humanitarian relief, and pursue a peaceful settlement through dialogue and negotiations.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will abstain on this draft. We strongly support the humanitarian objectives it invokes: safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and respect for international humanitarian law. But the Council cannot treat this crisis as though it arose without cause or without responsibility. Russia’s unprovoked aggression against Ukraine has created this humanitarian catastrophe. This draft fails to name the aggressor, fails to demand that Russia cease its attacks and withdraw its forces, and risks creating a false equivalence between the victim and the perpetrator. The United Kingdom remains fully committed to Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders. We will continue to support the work of humanitarian agencies and to insist that humanitarian access be genuine, principled and not used to facilitate forced displacement or deportation. For those reasons, we are not in a position to vote in favour of this text.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States supports the humanitarian objectives reflected in this text: safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and a cessation of hostilities. But this is not a serious or balanced humanitarian resolution. It refuses to name the aggressor or to demand that Russia stop its unprovoked and unjustified war and withdraw its forces from Ukraine. It places the victim and the aggressor on the same footing, and it omits any reaffirmation of the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. We sought in good faith to strengthen the text to reflect the reality of Russia’s assault on Ukraine, including the forcible displacement and deportation of civilians to Russia. Because those essential amendments were not accepted, the United States cannot support this resolution. We will abstain. We reiterate our call on Russia to immediately cease hostilities, withdraw its military forces, and allow safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and we will continue to stand with the people and Government of Ukraine.

after.China: Mr. President, China voted in favour of the draft resolution. We regret that it was not adopted. China’s position on the Ukraine issue is consistent and clear. We respect the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of all countries and believe that the Ukraine issue should be resolved through dialogue and negotiation. The humanitarian situation in Ukraine is grave, and the safety and legitimate rights of civilians must be effectively guaranteed. Humanitarian assistance should follow the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence and must not be politicized. We call on all parties to exercise restraint, cease hostilities as soon as possible, protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access. China supports the Secretary-General and relevant parties in continuing mediation efforts. We hope the Security Council will remain united and play a constructive role in promoting a ceasefire and a peaceful settlement.
after.Ghana:
Mr. President,

Ghana abstained on the draft resolution before the Council. We did so despite our full support for its humanitarian provisions. Ghana remains deeply concerned by the deteriorating humanitarian situation in Ukraine and the suffering of civilians. We support an immediate cessation of hostilities, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the voluntary and safe evacuation of civilians, and we reject forced displacement or deportation.

At the same time, Ghana believes that the Council must be clear and consistent in upholding the Charter. The text should have expressly reaffirmed the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders, and it should have clearly addressed the need for an end to the hostilities and the withdrawal of foreign forces so that a peaceful settlement can be pursued. Those omissions prevented us from supporting the text. We regret that the Council could not unite around a balanced humanitarian resolution, and we call on all parties to prioritize humanitarian access and dialogue. Ghana remains committed to the peaceful settlement of disputes and to respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States.
after.Russian Federation: Madam President, the Russian Federation has taken the floor after the vote to express our deep regret that this balanced humanitarian draft was not adopted. The text before the Council did not accuse anyone or advance a one-sided political agenda. It called for an immediate cessation of hostilities by all parties, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the voluntary and safe evacuation of civilians, and it expressly rejected forced displacement or deportation. That is precisely what a humanitarian resolution should do. We thank the Chinese delegation for its principled support and the co-sponsors for their constructive approach. Unfortunately, the delegations that abstained or voted against this draft made clear that their priorities are not humanitarian. They sought to turn the Council into an instrument of political pressure and to insert language that would have prejudged the situation and deepened confrontation. Their references to so-called “false equivalence” are a pretext. The Security Council should protect civilians, not serve as a platform for propaganda. We call on all members to stop politicizing humanitarian assistance and to support practical efforts, including humanitarian corridors, which Russia will continue to facilitate. The Russian Federation remains ready for constructive work on genuinely humanitarian issues.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United States abstained on this draft because it was not a serious humanitarian resolution. The humanitarian catastrophe in Ukraine is not a natural disaster or a neutral emergency. It is the direct consequence of President Putin’s unprovoked and unjustified war of choice against Ukraine. A text that refuses to name the aggressor, refuses to demand that Russia stop its attacks and withdraw its forces from Ukraine’s internationally recognized territory, and refuses to reaffirm Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity does not help the victims of this war; it obscures who is responsible for it.

We supported the humanitarian objectives contained in this text—safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and an end to hostilities. We sought in good faith to strengthen the text, including to address the forced displacement and deportation of Ukrainian civilians to Russia. Those efforts were not accepted. We cannot support a resolution that places the victim and the aggressor on the same footing.

The result of this vote is clear. Russia stands isolated. The Council has not adopted a text that fails to confront the reality of Russia’s war. The United States will continue to stand with Ukraine, to support humanitarian relief for those affected by Russia’s aggression, and to pursue accountability for violations of international humanitarian law. Russia must stop its war and withdraw its forces from Ukraine.
